html:
Dhofar, in the far south of Oman, is one of the few places where frankincense trees grow. Their resin was traded across the ancient world, and the ports of Sumhuram (Khor Rori) and later Al-Baleed shipped it for centuries.

Frankincense was burned in temples from Egypt to Rome and China. From Dhofar it went by sea, and by camel along the incense route up through Yemen and the Hejaz to the Mediterranean. Sumhuram was founded by the kingdom of Hadhramaut in Yemen.

The trade fell off after Rome became Christian, though it never quite ended. The groves, the oasis of Shisr and the ports became a World Heritage Site in 2000. See also Marib.
